ada lea.bio:
Ada Lea is the musical project of Montréal songwriter and visual artist Alexandra Levy, whose work turns everyday city life into sharply observed indie rock and folk-pop. Her 2019 debut, what we say in private, introduced a diaristic writing style willing to leave rough edges intact rather than resolve every feeling cleanly. On 2021's one hand on the steering wheel the other sewing a garden, Levy made Montréal itself part of the record's structure: songs move through streets, memories and relationships like points on a personal map, with arrangements that can shift from intimate folk to noisier, more unstable rock textures.

That second album deepened Ada Lea's international profile and established an ongoing collaboration with producer and drummer Marshall Vore. Levy followed it with the 2024 EP notes, a collection assembled from songs that sat between album cycles, before returning in 2025 with the 16-track when i paint my masterpiece. Recorded live and loosely with a small band in rural Ontario and produced with Luke Temple, the album widened her sound without abandoning the close-up detail of her writing. In 2026, the end is a wave extended that period with another set of songs, showing a catalogue developing through accumulation rather than dramatic reinvention.

Ada Lea matters within contemporary Canadian indie music because place, memory and process are not background details in her songs; they are part of the form. Her records connect Montréal's singer-songwriter tradition to a wider North American indie network while retaining a distinctly local sense of geography and observation. The result is music that rewards following the catalogue as a body of work, where recurring streets, relationships and images gradually build a larger emotional map.
ada lea.directory_summary: Montréal songwriter and visual artist Alexandra Levy records as Ada Lea, building intimate indie rock and folk-pop from memory, place and sharply observed city life. From what we say in private through one hand on the steering wheel the other sewing a garden and when i paint my masterpiece, her songs treat Montréal streets, relationships and recurring images as part of a larger emotional map rather than isolated snapshots.
album_titles: one hand on the steering wheel the other sewing a garden

8485.bio:
Toronto artist 8485, often called Eighty, emerged from the internet-native experimental pop community at the turn of the 2020s, bringing together hyperpop's digital abrasion with a more melodic, emotionally exposed songwriting style. Early releases including alpha testing and the 2021 EP plague town developed a cybernetic visual language around music that could jump between glitchy pop, emo, electronic production and heavier guitar-rooted instincts. The project grew alongside collaborators in the Helix Tears orbit, particularly producer blackwinterwells, while 8485's writing increasingly treated online identity as a framework for very human anxiety, attachment and self-scrutiny.

By 2023's Personal Protocol, 8485 had expanded that vocabulary into drum and bass, breakbeats and atmospheric dance-pop without losing the intimate writing at the centre of the project. The record was written and performed by 8485 and executive produced by blackwinterwells, with a wider group of underground producers contributing across its tracks. Her profile continued to widen through collaborations and live activity, including the 2025 single “G.I.R.L.” with Danny Brown and a guest appearance on Brown's Stardust, connecting a scene born largely through online networks to an established figure in experimental hip-hop.

8485's Canadian significance is less about conventional chart crossover than about representing a generation of Toronto music that developed simultaneously online and locally. Exclaim! has described her as a Toronto scene mainstay, while The FADER profiled her early as part of a digitally connected underground-pop movement. Her work shows how Canadian independent pop in the 2020s can build community, aesthetics and international reach without passing through the older radio-and-label pipeline first.
8485.directory_summary: Toronto's 8485 is an internet-native experimental pop artist whose catalogue moves through hyperpop, emo, drum and bass and atmospheric dance music without losing its emotionally direct core. Early releases such as plague town led into the broader electronic palette of Personal Protocol, while later work with Danny Brown connected her digitally grown scene to experimental hip-hop. She represents a distinctly 2020s route from Toronto's online underground to international attention.
